units.text: I have been lying under my sheets for three hours, frozen stiff in the dark.
It is five thirty in the morning, and the copper smell of blood in my bedroom is making me gag.
Across from my mattress, my parents are staring straight at me.
Their eyes never blink, and their mouths hang wide open in the shadows.
But they are not alive.
Something dragged them here.
And right now, that hairless thing is crouched directly beneath my bed, waiting for me to move.
Let us go back to the beginning.
It all began around two thirty in the morning.
I was asleep in my room when a sharp, jagged scream tore through the far end of the hallway.
I woke up in a cold sweat, sitting upright with my heart hammering against my ribs.
The house immediately fell dead silent again.
Not a floorboard creaked.
I told myself it was just a bad dream, but my stomach twisted with anxiety.
Before going to check on my parents, I realized I had to use the bathroom.
Looking back now, taking that detour might be the only reason I am still breathing.
I slipped out of my sheets and crept down the hallway on bare feet.
The bathroom was pitch black.
I did not dare turn on the overhead bulb, only letting in the faint grey light from the high window.
When I stepped back into the doorway, I felt a damp coldness against the carpet.
I looked down.
Heavy, dark streaks trailed from the master bedroom toward my door.
Pure terror seized my throat.
I did not scream.
I did not investigate.
Like a frightened child, I bolted back into my room and dove under my blankets, pulling the fabric over my eyes.
I squeezed my eyelids shut and prayed that the shadows were playing tricks on me.
I told myself morning was coming, and that dawn would wipe it all away.
Then, in the dead silence of the bedroom, my hinges began to groan.
The door slowly swung inward, stopping with a soft click against the frame.
I dared to pull the blanket down just enough to expose one eye into the dim room.
What stepped through the threshold was not human.
It was tall, hairless, and completely naked, with pale leathery skin pulled tight over its ribs.
Its spine was bent in a heavy hunch, and it possessed no eyes, only smooth, hollow sockets where sight should be.
Yet it moved with cold, calculating purpose.
In its long, sinewy arms, it was dragging my mother and father across the floor, completely limp and unresponsive.
I had to bite my own tongue until it bled to keep from screaming.
The creature did not toss them aside.
It began arranging them with sick, methodical care.
It hauled my father upright and propped him against the side of my bed, turning his head so his blank, unblinking eyes faced directly into mine.
Then it dragged my mother to the desk chair, seating her upright with her arms limp and her mouth gaping open toward me.
They looked like grotesque mannequins staged for an audience.
Next, the creature dipped its clawed fingers into the dark fluid pooling on the floor.
It began dragging its hands across my bedroom wall, painting thick, ritualistic symbols and a jagged circle around the mirror.
It was crafting what it considered its masterpiece.
At the center of the wall, it dragged its nails into the plaster, carving a line of words that I could not yet read in the pitch black.
When it finished, the creature turned slowly toward my mattress.
I held my breath, relaxing my muscles and pretending to be dead asleep.
It did not strike.
Instead, it sank down to all fours, slithering beneath the frame of my bed like a spider retreating into its hole.
I felt the wooden slats beneath my spine dip under its weight.
That was three hours ago.
Ever since, I have been trapped here, watching the clock tick from two thirty to five thirty.
I cannot twitch.
I cannot sneeze.
The second I show any sign of consciousness, I know its claws will tear up through the mattress.
I considered throwing the sheets and sprinting for the front door to scream for neighbors, but the creature is inches below my heels.
Over the past few hours, the sky outside my window has turned from ink black to a pale, misty pre-dawn grey.
The faint light has begun washing across the opposite wall.
Against my will, my gaze drifted back to the bloody inscription the creature had gouged into the plaster above my desk.
With my eyes fully adjusted to the morning twilight, every single word became sharp and legible.
It was not a ritual chant.
It was four simple words meant only for me.
It read: I know you are awake.
This story was inspired by I Know You're Awake, as published in creepypasta archives.
Now tell me.
Would you have looked under the bed?
